headline: The S&P gave up 1.2% while the AI complex gave up 7 - and the 17bp belly rally that paid for it came with MOVE +11.4%, which is a growth scare, not relief.
summary: Yesterday's beta binge got liquidated from the inside. SPX -1.2% to 7663, but NDX -2.9%, SOXX -6.8% (z=-1.99, acceleration z=-1.93), SMH -6.0%, AMD -8.1%, MU -6.3%, ASML -6.9%, NVDA -4.4%, META -7.0% with acceleration z=-2.93. Against that, the Dow was flat, RSP +0.7%, IWM +0.1%, XLP +3.3% (z=2.28), SPLV +2.2%, XLU +2.1%, KRE +2.5%, ITB +5.4%, LMT +7.0%, BX +8.4%. High-beta/low-vol fell 7.0% in a single session to z=-2.52 with acceleration z=-2.49 - the single largest dislocation on the board - while RSP/SPY rose 1.9% with acceleration z=3.01. This is not a market-wide de-risking; it is the AI trade being sold to fund everything else. QQQ/SPY -1.7% with acceleration z=-2.29, IWF/IWD -3.1%, MTUM -3.7%, SMH/SPY z=-2.23.

The bond rally is the tell, and it is not dovish. Two-year 4.65% (-16bp), five-year 4.78% (-17bp), ten-year back under 5% at 4.96% (-17bp), 10y real yield 2.64% (-12bp), TLT +1.9%. Yet MOVE jumped 11.4% to 106.84, z=1.93, acceleration z=1.03, now 39.7% above its 200-day and +36% on the month. Yields fall and bond vol explodes only when the move is a flight, not a repricing of policy. The inflation split confirms it: 5-year breakevens +5bp to 2.45% (+13bp on the month, z=0.56) while 10-year breakevens fell 5bp to 2.32%. Near-term inflation up, long-term growth down. Brent +3.8% to 112.96, +13.8% on the month and 91st percentile, with WTI only 99.07 - the grade spread widened to ~$13.9. Oil/gold +4.6%, 97th percentile. The inflation composite deteriorated to -44 from -30 yesterday; rates improved only marginally to -56. Risk regime -24 from -18.

Where the money went matters as much as where it left. Healthcare at the 100th percentile of its year (XLV +1.3%, relative strength +8.0% on the month, acceleration z=1.63; LLY +2.8%, UNH +1.9%), staples relative strength +10.1%, USMV and IWD at the 100th percentile, insurance KIE +2.0% with acceleration z=1.51, banks KBE +2.4% and KRE/SPY +3.8%. Rate-sensitives caught the yield move hard: DHI +6.2%, ITB +5.4%, HD +4.3%, XRT +2.9% - even though the 30-year mortgage is still 7.32%, +37bp on the month, 94th percentile. Credit has not broken: HYG +0.2%, LQD +1.0%, BKLN -0.1%. But HYG/IEF fell 0.9% to z=-1.49 - junk is getting left behind by Treasuries, which is exactly how credit lags a growth scare. Front vol is no longer the cheap hedge it was yesterday: VIX +14.1% to 19.03, VIX3M +7.5% to 20.12, term structure 0.946 from 0.891, z=1.95 with acceleration z=1.30. Take profit on front-dated hedges; roll out.

The hard-asset complex split in two. Crude rips while everything else liquidates: gold -2.5% to 4044 (6th percentile, z=-1.81), silver -4.8%, platinum -3.3%, GDXJ -6.7%, GDX -5.8% (-16.5% on the month), copper -2.0%, COPX -6.3%, XME -4.6% and 15.0% below its 200-day, FCX -6.3%. Gold/silver +2.4% with acceleration z=1.37 keeps flagging stress inside the metals. The AI-power-and-grid complex was annihilated again: GEV -10.6%, VST -9.8%, ETN -6.3% (z=-2.45), CEG -5.7%, GRID -4.3%, NLR -18.9% and URA -22.1% on the month, REMX -27.3%. Offshore, EM relative strength broke: EEM -2.9% with EEM/SPY z=-2.39, EWY -5.0% (-22.6% on the month), EWT -4.6%, KWEB -2.2%, FXI -1.5%, and USDMXN +1.6% to a 100th-percentile 18.71 with z=3.17 and acceleration z=1.70. Brazil remains the one clean long abroad: EWZ +9.4% on the month, 13.3% above its 200-day, with the real still firm at 5.05.

good.text: The belly of the curve rallied hard: 2y -16bp to 4.65%, 5y -17bp, 10y -17bp back under 5.00% at 4.96%, 10y real yield -12bp to 2.64%, TLT +1.9%. Every discount-rate-sensitive asset got relief.
Breadth improved while the index fell - the opposite of a classic down day. RSP/SPY +1.9% with acceleration z=3.01, equal-weight +0.7%, Dow flat, IWM +0.1% versus SPX -1.2%.
Credit refused to confirm the equity stress: HYG +0.2%, LQD +1.0%, BKLN -0.1%. No spread event today, just an equity-factor unwind.
Financials led: XLF +1.1%, KRE +2.5%, KBE +2.4%, KIE +2.0% with acceleration z=1.51, KRE/SPY +3.8%. A steeper front end and no credit event is their best setup in months.
Defensive quality is making highs, not just holding: XLV at the 100th percentile with relative strength +8.0% on the month, LLY +2.8%, UNH +1.9%, XLP +3.3% (z=2.28), USMV at the 100th percentile.
Rate-sensitive cyclicals caught a real bid: ITB +5.4%, XHB +3.8%, DHI +6.2%, HD +4.3%, XRT +2.9%. The consumer tape is not acting like a recession yet.

bad.text: The semiconductor de-rating went vertical: SOXX -6.8% (z=-1.99, acceleration z=-1.93), SMH -6.0%, AMD -8.1%, MU -6.3%, ASML -6.9%, TSM -4.5%, NVDA -4.4%. SMH/SPY z=-2.23 and still rolling over.
Beta was dumped at a pace that is itself the warning: SPHB/SPLV -7.0% in one day, z=-2.52, acceleration z=-2.49; MTUM -3.7%, IWF/IWD -3.1%, QQQ/SPY acceleration z=-2.29, ARKK -4.2%, IPO -4.4%.
Bond vol exploded on a yield rally - MOVE +11.4% to 106.84, z=1.93, acceleration z=1.03, 39.7% above its 200-day. Falling yields plus rising vol is flight, not easing.

The supply shock keeps compounding: Brent +3.8% to 112.96 (+13.8% on the month, 91st percentile), oil/gold +4.6% at the 97th percentile, DBC at the 99th, 5y breakevens +5bp to 2.45%, mortgage 7.32%. The inflation composite worsened to -44 from -30.
The AI power/capex complex was taken apart again: GEV -10.6%, VST -9.8%, ETN -6.3% (z=-2.45), CEG -5.7%, GRID -4.3%, NLR -18.9% and URA -22.1% on the month, REMX -27.3%.

EM relative strength broke and the peso is a 3-sigma problem: EEM -2.9% with EEM/SPY z=-2.39, EWY -5.0%, EWT -4.6%, FXI -1.5%, USDMXN +1.6% to 18.71 with z=3.17 and acceleration z=1.70 at the 100th percentile.

trades.name: Low-vol over high-beta
trades.line: Long SPLV vs short SPHB - the beta unwind is accelerating
trades.expr: Long SPLV, short SPHB, dollar-neutral. Size the short slightly smaller for beta, or substitute USMV long vs QQQ short for a more liquid version.
trades.thesis: The index is being hollowed out from the top: defensives and equal-weight absorb the flows while high-beta, momentum and growth are liquidated. This rotation is being driven by a de-rating of the AI capex complex, not by a credit or macro event, so it can run for weeks without the index collapsing.
trades.trigger: SPHB/SPLV -7.0% in one session to z=-2.52 with acceleration z=-2.49 and a rolling-over trend; SPLV +2.2% with acceleration z=2.05, USMV at the 100th percentile of its year, RSP/SPY acceleration z=3.01.
trades.stop: SPHB/SPLV recovers above 1.90 (a >5% reversal) or VIX closes back below 16 with SOXX reclaiming its recent high.
trades.target: SPHB/SPLV toward 1.65, roughly 8% further, over the next month.

trades.name: Software over semis
trades.line: Long IGV vs short SOXX - software over semis
trades.expr: Long IGV, short SOXX (or SMH) in equal dollars. Express the short with Jan SOXX put spreads if you want defined risk after a 6.8% day.
trades.thesis: The AI trade is bifurcating: recurring-revenue software is holding while the capital-intensive silicon and power layer de-rates. IGV/SMH is already +18.2% on the month and the spread is still accelerating, which is how regime shifts in leadership look at the start, not the end.
trades.trigger: IGV/SMH +6.3% today to z=2.63 with acceleration z=2.12 and a turning-up trend, while SOXX -6.8% with acceleration z=-1.93 and SMH/SPY z=-2.23. IGV was down only 0.1% on the day.
trades.stop: IGV/SMH back below 0.195 (a ~6% give-back) or SOXX reclaiming 520 with AMD and MU making new highs.

trades.name: AI power capex
trades.line: Short GEV - the AI power capex trade is unwinding
trades.expr: Short GEV outright, or buy 3-month puts ~10% out of the money. Fund with a long XLU leg if you want to isolate merchant/capex from regulated utilities.
trades.thesis: The power-for-AI theme is being priced out across the entire chain, from turbines to grid gear to fuel. This is the second derivative of the semiconductor de-rating: if datacenter capex slows, the backlog multiple on the electrical complex goes first.
trades.trigger: GEV -10.6% today and -12.9% on the month, z=-1.52, 11.6% below its 200-day; VST -9.8%, ETN -6.3% (z=-2.45), CEG -5.7%, GRID -4.3%, NLR -18.9% on the month, URA -22.1%. Meanwhile XLU +2.1% - regulated is fine, capex is not.
trades.stop: GEV closes back above its 200-day near 936, or NLR and GRID both turn up with semis.

trades.name: 5-year breakevens
trades.line: Long 5y breakevens via TIP vs IEF - $113 Brent isn't priced
trades.expr: Buy 5-year TIPS against 5-year nominals in equal duration. ETF proxy: long TIP, short IEF, duration-matched.
trades.thesis: The market is pricing a growth scare in nominals and refusing to pay for the energy shock. Brent is up 13.8% in a month and 85.6% on the year and the five-year breakeven is only at the 52nd percentile of its own range. Either the belly rally is wrong or breakevens are too low; this trade wins in both the stagflation and the supply-shock path and only loses if crude breaks.
trades.trigger: 5y breakeven +5bp today to 2.45% (+13bp on the month, z=0.56, acceleration 0.48) while the 10y breakeven fell 5bp to 2.32% and nominal 5y yields fell 17bp. Brent 112.96, DBC at the 99th percentile, oil/gold at the 97th, CPI index z=0.65 with acceleration 0.61.
trades.stop: 5y breakeven below 2.30%, or Brent back under $100.

trades.name: Brazil over Mexico
trades.line: Long EWZ vs short EWW - Brazil over Mexico, real over peso
trades.expr: Long EWZ, short EWW in equal dollars. Purer FX version: short MXN vs long BRL spot.
trades.thesis: Both LatAm equity markets are up on the month in local terms, but only one is paying dollar investors. The peso has gone from carry darling to a three-sigma unwind, which eats every point the Bolsa makes; the real is firm and Brazilian equities are in a genuine uptrend with the best relative strength on the global board.
trades.trigger: USDMXN +1.6% today to 18.71, +8.7% on the month, z=3.17 with acceleration z=1.70 at the 100th percentile - while MXX is +8.4% on the month and EWW captured only +0.7%. Brazil: BVSP +8.9% on the month (z=1.45), EWZ +9.4% and 13.3% above its 200-day, USDBRL -1.1%.
trades.stop: USDMXN back below 18.00, or EWZ breaking its 200-day (~36.9).
trades.target: 10% on the pair over three months.

trades.name: Fade the housing pop
trades.line: Short ITB - fade the mortgage-rate relief pop at 7.32%
trades.expr: Short ITB into the spike, or buy Dec/Jan ITB puts. Keep it small - this is a counter-trend fade of a one-day move.
trades.thesis: Builders ripped on a 17bp Treasury rally, but the actual funding cost of a house is 7.32% and still 37bp higher than a month ago at the 94th percentile of the year. A growth scare that lowers the ten-year but keeps mortgage spreads wide is not a housing recovery; it is weaker demand at the same price.
trades.trigger: ITB +5.4% and XHB +3.8% today with XHB/SPY +5.0% (acceleration z=1.01), yet both ETFs remain in downtrends, ITB 4.6% below its 200-day at the 27th percentile, and the 30-year mortgage at 7.32% with z=1.10.
trades.stop: ITB closes above its 200-day near 95.7, or the 30-year mortgage prints below 7.00%.
